question: What is the primary medical term for a low salt diet?
explanation: A low salt diet is formally called a sodium-restricted diet because it specifically limits sodium intake. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h1)

question: Why is a low salt diet frequently prescribed in clinical practice?

options.A: To prevent sudden drops in blood sugar
options.B: To stimulate a faster metabolic rate
options.C: To reduce strain on the heart and blood vessels
options.D: To increase the body's overall fluid retention

explanation: Excess salt causes water retention which raises blood pressure, so restricting salt lightens the workload on the cardiovascular system. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h1)

question: Where is sodium mostly found in the body, making it a key electrolyte?
explanation: You've got this! Sodium is a positively charged ion that stays mostly in the fluid outside of our cells, which is why it's called an extracellular cation.

question: What happens to blood volume when sodium levels rise in the blood?

options.A: Blood volume drops rapidly through increased sweating
options.B: Blood volume decreases because sodium repels water
options.C: Blood volume stays the same because cells absorb the excess
options.D: Blood volume increases because water follows sodium

explanation: Sodium exerts strong osmotic pressure, meaning water is drawn toward areas with higher sodium concentration, thereby increasing total fluid volume. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h2)

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?
explanation: Hypertension is directly linked to sodium intake, making salt restriction a primary medical intervention for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with severe heart failure and fluid accumulation in the lungs. Why is a low salt diet ordered?

options.A: To prevent further fluid retention and reduce cardiac workload
options.B: To improve digestion and absorption of oral medications
options.C: To stimulate red blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: To cure the underlying viral infection in the heart muscle

explanation: Restricting salt stops the body from holding onto extra water, which lessens the volume of blood the weakened heart has to pump. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h3)

question: What is the approximate percentage of sodium found in table salt by weight?
explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, which breaks down to about 40 percent sodium and 60 percent chloride. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h4)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to distinguish between table salt and pure sodium when teaching patients?

options.A: One gram of table salt contains much less than one gram of actual sodium
options.B: Pure sodium is a liquid while table salt is a heavy solid rock
options.C: Table salt contains no sodium at all until it is cooked in oil
options.D: Patients can eat unlimited table salt if they avoid processed foods

explanation: Because salt is only 40 percent sodium, patients often miscalculate their total daily intake if they treat salt and sodium as identical measurements. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h4)

question: Which item is a major source of hidden sodium in many Nigerian home-cooked meals?
explanation: Seasoning cubes are packed with sodium and are frequently added in multiple quantities to local soups and stews. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h5)

question: A patient with hypertension insists they stopped adding salt to their food at the table, yet their blood pressure remains high. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: They are drinking too much plain clean water throughout the day
options.B: They are likely consuming hidden sodium from stock cubes, canned fish, and condiments
options.C: They have stopped taking their prescribed medications completely
options.D: They are eating too many fresh, raw fruits from the local market

explanation: Table salt is only part of the intake; hidden sodium in processed seasonings and preserved ingredients can easily ruin a low-salt regimen. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h5)

question: What is a safe, effective substitute to enhance flavor without adding sodium?

options.A: Fresh garlic, ginger, and local herbs
options.C: Extra helpings of commercial seasoning cubes
options.D: Table salt mixed with white sugar

explanation: Aromatics like garlic and ginger provide strong flavors and aromas that compensate for a lack of salt. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h6)

question: Why is cooking with fresh, whole ingredients emphasized in a low-sodium meal plan?

options.A: It guarantees that the food will cook in half the usual time
options.B: It destroys all natural vitamins found in local tubers and vegetables
options.C: It allows the person preparing the food to control the exact amount of sodium added
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any water during the boiling process

explanation: Processed foods come pre-loaded with sodium, whereas raw, whole ingredients contain only natural, trace amounts of sodium. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h6)

question: What happens to a patient's taste buds after a few weeks of following a low salt diet?

options.A: They gradually adjust, making foods taste flavorful with less salt
options.B: They permanently lose the ability to taste warm foods
options.C: They demand twice as much salt to feel any satisfaction
options.D: They become completely numb to all sweet and bitter tastes

explanation: Taste buds adapt over time, meaning food that initially tastes bland will eventually become satisfying as the palate resets. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h7)

question: Why is it important to include family members in dietary education for a patient requiring a low salt diet?

options.A: Family members are the ones who administer oral medications at home
options.B: Family members are legally responsible for paying hospital medical bills
options.C: Family members must also follow the exact same medical diagnosis
options.D: Family members usually prepare the meals and must support the dietary changes

explanation: In many homes, cooking is shared or done by someone other than the patient, so family buy-in ensures the right food gets cooked. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h7)

question: What physical sign should a nurse check for when assessing a patient for fluid overload due to excess salt intake?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Pitting edema in the ankles and shins
options.C: Extreme dryness and cracking of the lips
options.D: Rapid thinning of the fingernail beds

explanation: Fluid retention from excess sodium pooling in the lower extremities commonly presents as pitting edema over bony prominences. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h8)

question: Why is daily weight tracking important for a patient with heart failure on a sodium-restricted diet?

options.A: Sudden weight gain often signals dangerous fluid retention from excess salt
options.B: It measures how fast the patient's muscle mass is growing
options.C: It proves the patient is eating enough calories to prevent malnutrition
options.D: It determines the exact dosage of vitamins needed each week

explanation: Because water weight accumulates rapidly when sodium is high, daily scale readings give an early warning before severe symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T007#GNS227_U6_T007_h8)
